## splitBraces() function

Applies the selected Go syntax.SplitBraces operation synchronously to a mutable Word and returns its exact boolean. First use initializes WASM synchronously. `true` does not imply that a BraceExp exists: malformed or singleton brace text can return true while being represented again as literals. No fields expand.

The Word keeps its identity. False preserves its Parts array and children; true replaces Parts as Go does, retaining input WordPart objects that Go reuses, including inside new brace elements. Newly split literals retain Go's copied position values; new nodes have no entry in an original PositionSnapshot. Existing aliases to an old Parts array continue to observe that old array. Selected Go Walk rejects BraceExp nodes; callers can inspect the transformed records directly. This operation does not extend traversal's supported nodes.

InputError identifies unrepresentable input. A panic from the selected native operation becomes ShInternalError and leaves the supplied Word unchanged. Native output has a separate bridge limit of 256 nested Go struct records, checked iteratively after rewriting and before recursive transport. This can refuse a valid Go result with ShInternalError; it is not parser work or grammar. JavaScript input/output stack exhaustion also becomes ShInternalError with its original RangeError as `cause`<!-- -->. Both refusals leave the supplied Word unchanged. No fixed depth acceptance or arbitrary caller-stack guarantee follows. An unexpected native engine stack trap also retains its cause, but adaptation alone does not establish the health of the native runtime after such a trap. This operation does not change parser output before explicitly being called.

